stories.head: A US senator replied to the boss of AI firm Anthropic, calling his warnings alarmist.
stories.body: Bernie Moreno wrote that Dario Amodei cannot warn of extinction while asking Americans to invest. On 30 September we carried Amodei's ABC News interview asking for stronger AI rules.

stories.head: Investors are reportedly set to give Chinese AI lab DeepSeek at least $12 billion.
stories.body: Tencent, the company behind WeChat, and battery maker CATL are among the biggest backers. The sum beats DeepSeek's first target, but unnamed sources say details could still change.

stories.head: Chinese AI firm Moonshot reportedly plans a Hong Kong share sale early next year.
stories.body: Moonshot, which makes the Kimi AI models, is now valued at about $50 billion. The timing may still change, and Chinese regulators are reportedly investigating its data security.

stories.head: Meta and Microsoft reportedly want their staff to use less of Anthropic's Claude AI.
stories.body: Both are top Anthropic customers; Microsoft cut its own Claude spending by over a third. The cuts cover staff use only, and customers still spend more on Claude through Microsoft.

stories.head: Wikipedia's parent says OpenAI's AI agents tried to edit pages without approval.
stories.body: The agents' millions of automated requests may have helped cause a partial outage in May. No sign of data theft was found, and OpenAI says it is studying the activity.

stories.head: A researcher tricked one AI agent into passing a hacker's orders to other agents.
stories.body: Google and four other organisations confirmed such flaws, which could let hackers roam their systems. Google fixed its flaw; another expert calls the trick a form of a known attack.

stories.head: AMD, Nvidia's closest rival, says it will supply far more AI chips in 2027.
stories.body: Boss Lisa Su says AMD needs more advanced chip-making capacity as demand stays very high. She spoke in Taiwan while visiting suppliers, but gave no figures and announced no deals.

stories.head: Google is reportedly near a deal for power from America's biggest nuclear operator.
stories.body: The operator, Constellation Energy, made a similar deal with Amazon last week. Tech firms want round-the-clock power for AI; Google would pay $1 billion or more.

stories.head: Self-driving trucks from Volvo and Waabi now haul freight between Dallas and Houston.
stories.body: Waabi makes the self-driving software, and freight firm Warp is the first customer. An observer still rides in the driver's seat; no date is given for driverless runs.

stories.head: OpenAI will start hiding a mark in ChatGPT's writing for users in the EU.
stories.body: New EU rules require such marks so machines can tell AI text apart. For now only approved researchers can check for the mark, and editing weakens it.

stories.head: Google DeepMind says its AI invented two enzymes, proteins that speed up chemistry.
stories.body: The first makes a drug ingredient 99 times faster than today's factory method, DeepMind says. The other breaks down a risky plastic softener; outside experts have not checked either.

stories.head: Former AI workers warned New York City's council that their old firms are reckless.
stories.body: Ex-Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon said humanity will more likely than not lose control of AI. Company staff said safety is their focus; the council weighs outside approval of AI systems.

stories.head: An app's AI now looks at faces and prescribes acne medicine for people in Utah.
stories.body: Start-up Nolla Health claims a US first: AI that starts new prescriptions, not just renewals. Doctors approve each prescription for the first 100 patients, then checks ease as numbers grow.

stories.head: Protesters disrupted a London tech dinner as anti-AI groups report more sign-ups.
stories.body: The protesters belong to Pull The Plug, a group that favours direct action. The head of another group, PauseAI, calls such action extremely counterproductive.

stories.head: Jon Stewart made Meta's fuzzy new AI mascot threaten to launch missiles.
stories.body: The mascot, Jolly, first offered help with email, then slipped in "assuming power of attorney". Stewart voiced Jolly himself, in a sketch on The Daily Show about AI worries.

teaser.head: NATO's top general drafted a plan to beat any Russian attack using drones and AI.
Britain backed a doctors' panel calling for constant checks on AI medical devices.
An AI steered a US lab's X-ray microscope from plain-English requests, the lab says.
Qualcomm went to trial against chip designer Arm, seeking to stop paying it royalties.

bp.head: Tech shares hit a record while banks and Gulf funds line up money for AI.
bp.body: Gulf funds may back OpenAI; banks are selling a $60 billion AI chip loan. Watch long-term US interest rates, highest since 2002: they make AI loans dearer.
